input: Draft a bucket list for my fortieth birthday year

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the list should cover one symbolic birthday day, the calendar year, or the full year from birthday to birthday determines how ambitious and wide-ranging the items should be.
Whether items are solo adventures, couple experiences, family activities, or friend group events completely changes the nature of the entries on the list.
The user's current life situation — where they live, whether they can travel internationally, family commitments — shapes what is realistically possible to include.
Budget available for the year heavily influences whether items lean toward big-ticket travel and experiences or low-cost personal challenges and milestones.

Understanding the balance the user wants — adventure vs. reflection, physical challenges vs. creative pursuits, ticking off classics vs. deeply personal goals — determines the tone and content of every item.
Knowing whether the user wants a short, curated list of 10 meaningful things or a sprawling list of 40 items (one per year of life) defines the structure and depth of the final output.
The desired format — a simple written list, a categorised document, a printable keepsake, a shared digital doc — determines how the draft should be structured and delivered.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a bucket list for my fortieth birthday year
gold.taskDescription: Create a personalised bucket list of experiences, goals, and milestones to accomplish during the user's fortieth birthday year.

questions.title: Does the year start on your birthday or January 1st?
questions.description: Clarify whether the bucket list window runs from the user's 40th birthday to their 41st, or covers a calendar year, to set the right time horizon.

questions.title: Are these experiences mostly solo, or shared with others?
questions.description: Determine whether the list should feature solo personal goals, couple/partner experiences, family activities, or a mix with friends, to tailor every entry accordingly.

questions.title: How much international or long-distance travel is realistic?
questions.description: Understand the user's travel freedom — passport, visa access, time off work, family ties — so items are geographically achievable rather than wishful.

questions.title: What is the rough total budget you have in mind?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is planning a modest, moderate, or generous spend for the year, so big-ticket items are included only where appropriate.

questions.title: What mix of experience types matters most to you?
questions.description: Find out whether the user leans toward physical challenges, creative projects, travel, relationships, career goals, or personal reflection, to shape the character of the list.

questions.title: How many items do you want on the final list?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a tight, curated shortlist (e.g. 10 items) or a fuller set (e.g. 40 items to mark each year of life), to set the right scope and ambition level.

questions.title: What format should the finished bucket list take?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a plain written list, a categorised document, a printable keepsake layout, or a shareable digital format, to deliver it in the most useful form.
